context.title: The New Covenant
context.summary: God promises everlasting love: Israel will dance again, Rachel's weeping for her lost children will end, and the exiles will come home. Then He announces a new covenant, writing His law on hearts and remembering sin no more.
context.background: Rachel, mother of Joseph and Benjamin, was buried near Bethlehem (Genesis 35:19); Ramah, north of Jerusalem, was where captives were gathered for deportation (40:1). Matthew 2:17-18 applies her weeping to Herod's slaughter at Bethlehem. Hebrews 8:8-12 quotes vv. 31–34 in full, often noted as the longest Old Testament quotation in the New Testament.

customs.note: A proverb blaming children's suffering on their parents' sins. Ezekiel 18:2 quotes it too. God says each person will answer for his own sin.

watchFor: The law written 'in their hearts' (v. 33), not on stone.
God's covenant is as fixed as sun, moon and stars (vv. 35–37).

people.name: Ephraim
people.summary: Double fruitfulness (“for God had made him fruitful in the land of his affliction”). The second son of Joseph, born in Egypt (Gen. 41:52; 46:20).

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

people.name: Rachel
people.summary: Ewe, “the daughter”, “the somewhat petulant, peevish, and self-willed though beautiful younger daughter” of Laban, and one of Jacob’s wives (Gen. 29:6, 28).

people.name: Gareb
people.summary: One of David’s warriors (2 Sam. 23:38), an Ithrite.

places.name: Samaria
places.summary: A watch-mountain or a watch-tower. In the heart of the mountains of Israel, a few miles north-west of Shechem, stands the “hill of Shomeron,” a solitary mountain, a great “mamelon.”

places.name: Zion
places.summary: Sunny; height, one of the eminences on which Jerusalem was built. It was surrounded on all sides, except the north, by deep valleys, that of the Tyropoeon separating it from Moriah, which it surpasses in height by 105 feet.

places.name: Ramah
places.summary: A city first mentioned in Josh. 18:25, near Gibeah of Benjamin. It was fortified by Baasha, king of Israel (1 Kings 15:17-22; 2 Chr. 16:1-6).

places.name: Egypt
places.summary: The land of the Nile and the pyramids, the oldest kingdom of which we have any record, holds a place of great significance in Scripture.

places.name: Tower
places.summary: God has graciously given, a tower in the wall of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:1; 12:39).

places.name: Gareb
places.summary: A hill near Jerusalem (Jer. 31:39), probably the hill of lepers, and consequently a place outside the boundary of the city.

places.name: Goah
places.summary: A lowing, a place near Jerusalem, mentioned only in Jer. 31:39.

places.name: horse gate
places.summary: A gate in the wall of Jerusalem, at the west end of the bridge, leading from Zion to the temple (Neh. 3:28; Jer. 31:40).

places.name: Kidron
places.summary: Kedron = Cedron, turbid, the winter torrent which flows through the Valley of Jehoshaphat, on the eastern side of Jerusalem, between the city and the Mount of Olives.

events.title: Prophecies of Jeremiah
events.summary: Passage: Jeremiah 1:1–52:34. People: Jeremiah. Lasted about 67 years.
